prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 重点城市季度GDP增速对比表 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "城市" spans 1 col × 2 row; "季度增速（%）" spans 4 col × 1 row; "说明" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "城市" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 35px
  col 2: header "季度增速（%） › 一季度" · longest unbreakable word 25px · one-line width 53px
  col 3: header "季度增速（%） › 二季度" · longest unbreakable word 25px · one-line width 53px
  col 4: header "季度增速（%） › 三季度" · longest unbreakable word 25px · one-line width 53px
  col 5: header "季度增速（%） › 四季度" · longest unbreakable word 25px · one-line width 53px
  col 6: header "说明" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 867px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 480px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 479px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 480px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"对比六个重点城市四个季度的GDP增速，并结合说明理解各城市的经济表现。","reading":"读者主要横向比较同一城市的季度变化，也会纵向比较不同城市在同一季度的增速；说明提供背景，通常在发现差异后阅读。说明文字较长，会主导各数据行的高度，因此城市名和增速可以利用同一行已有的高度保持清晰。","groups":["第2至第5列都是季度增速，作用相同，应保持相同宽度，便于横向和纵向比较。","第1列城市名标识整行；第6列说明为该城市的增速提供背景。"],"keep_intact":["城市名称","各季度的增速数值","百分比符号"],"may_wrap":["说明中的中文叙述可自然换行。","空间紧张时，季度子表头可换行；四列应采用一致的宽度和换行节奏。","跨四列的总表头可在必要时换行。"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[56,74,74,74,74,127],"idea":"优先保证城市名和季度子表头完整显示，四个季度等宽，说明列较窄并承担较多换行。"},{"name":"B","widths":[56,65,65,65,65,163],"idea":"在季度比较和说明阅读之间折中，四个季度表头一致换行，为说明提供更多空间。"},{"name":"C","widths":[56,54,54,54,54,207],"idea":"优先给长说明分配宽度，四个季度列仍等宽且数值完整，但季度表头需要换行。"}]}
